zero_omission_notes.summary: This chapter covers computational logic, height-ordering line puzzles, integer parity algebra (even/odd addition and multiplication rules), Virahāṅka-Fibonacci growth rules, cryptarithms, and magic square properties.

detailed_sections.full_notes: Children in line state how many people ahead are taller. Analyzing callout sequences allows uniquely constructing relative height order.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Callout Logic
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Callout count = number of standing individuals ahead strictly taller.

detailed_sections.full_notes: Parity defines whether an integer is even (2n) or odd (2n-1). Rules: Even + Even = Even; Odd + Odd = Even; Even + Odd = Odd. Even * Anything = Even; Odd * Odd = Odd.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Loose Sheet Parity
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Page numbers on a two-sided leaf are 2k-1 and 2k. Their sum 4k-1 is always ODD.

detailed_sections.full_notes: 3x3 Magic Square using digits 1-9: Constant sum = 15; Center square must be 5. Exactly 8 unique rotations/reflections exist.

master_glossary_units_and_formulas.definition_or_meaning: The property of an integer being even or odd
The invariant sum of each row, column, and diagonal (15 for 1-9)
Sum of two pages on one leaf (2k-1 + 2k = 4k-1) is always odd

textbook_exercises.question: Can the sum of page numbers of 50 loose sheets torn from a book be 6000?
textbook_exercises.answer: Each loose sheet has pages 2k-1 and 2k, whose sum is 4k-1 (odd). The sum of 50 odd numbers is always EVEN. Sum of first 100 pages = 5050. Any 50 sheets from 100 pages equals 5050. Thus, for a 100-page book it is 5050; for larger books, parity is even, so 6000 is mathematically possible in total parity terms.

objective_questions_1_mark.question: The first person in a line always calls out 0.
objective_questions_1_mark.explanation: Nobody stands ahead of the first person.

short_answer_questions.question: Determine parity of: Sum of 3 odd numbers and 2 even numbers.
short_answer_questions.answer: Odd + Odd + Odd = Odd. Even + Even = Even. Total = Odd + Even = Odd.

analytical_reasoning_questions.question: Prove why the center cell of a 3x3 magic square of numbers 1-9 must be 5.
analytical_reasoning_questions.answer: Sum 1..9 = 45. Row sum = 15. The center cell 'x' is part of 4 lines (row 2, col 2, two diagonals). Adding these 4 lines yields 4*15 = 60. In this sum, every cell is counted once, except x which is counted 4 times: 45 + 3x = 60 => 3x = 15 => x = 5.

comprehensive_long_answers.question: Explain parity rules for addition and multiplication of even and odd integers with algebraic proofs.
comprehensive_long_answers.answer:
1. Addition of two odds: (2m+1) + (2n+1) = 2m + 2n + 2 = 2(m+n+1) which is Even.
2. Addition of even and odd: (2m) + (2n+1) = 2(m+n) + 1 which is Odd.
3. Multiplication of two odds: (2m+1)(2n+1) = 4mn + 2m + 2n + 1 = 2(2mn+m+n) + 1 which is Odd.

competency_and_case_studies.case_scenario: A group of 8 people line up in single file.

qa.question: What is the maximum callout number possible in this group?
qa.answer: Maximum callout = 7, achieved by the shortest person standing at the very end when all 7 ahead are taller.

common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.common_error_or_misconception: Assuming the tallest person in a group must stand at the front of the line.
common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.correct_fact_or_method: The tallest person calls out 0 regardless of where they stand in line.
